title: Prime membership in a finite projective module is detected at the prime localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $N$ a finite projective $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], $s\in N$, and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal. Put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $N_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}N$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], with canonical map $N\to N_{\mathfrak p}$; write $R_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $s/1\in\mathfrak pN_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $s\in\mathfrak pN$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), together with localization and quotient exactness

proof.text: Since N is finite, choose a surjection $\pi:R^n\twoheadrightarrow N$. The lifting clause of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] lifts $\operatorname{id}_N$ along $\pi$, giving an $R$-linear map $i:N\to R^n$ with $\pi\circ i=\operatorname{id}_N$. Localizing at $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives maps $i_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\pi_{\mathfrak p}$ with $\pi_{\mathfrak p}\circ i_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{id}_{N_{\mathfrak p}}$.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 05CE and Lemma Tag 05CF (projective modules as direct summands), together with the finite-generation clause in Lemma Tag 00NX

proof.text: For the forward implication, if $s/1\in\mathfrak pN_{\mathfrak p}$, then applying $i_{\mathfrak p}$ gives $i(s)/1\in\mathfrak p(R^n)_{\mathfrak p}$ because $i_{\mathfrak p}$ is $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linear. By [lem-sc-free-prime-membership], $i(s)\in\mathfrak pR^n$; applying $\pi$ gives $s=\pi(i(s))\in\mathfrak pN$. Conversely, if $s\in\mathfrak pN$, the canonical localization map sends this relation to $s/1\in\mathfrak pN_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective), localization and direct-summand argument in the proof

proof_origin.place: Algebra, Tags 05CE/05CF and 00NX: direct-summand description of finite projectives and the localization membership calculation
